record.paper_title: Distinct Distances: Open Problems and Current Bounds
record.original_question: Using the same definition of phi(n,k,l), determine the asymptotic order of phi(n,3,3). Equivalently, determine the minimum number of distinct distances in an n-point planar set with no isosceles triangle, including degenerate ones with three collinear vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let $D(P)$ denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of $P$. Three points $a,b,c\in P$ are said to span an isosceles triangle if at least two of the three distances $|ab|,|bc|,|ca|$ are equal; this includes the degenerate case in which $a,b,c$ are collinear (so a triple with two equal distances among collinear points still counts as an isosceles triangle).

Define
$$\varphi(n,3,3) \;=\; \min\bigl\{\,D(P)\,:\, P\subset\mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n,\ \text{no three points of }P\text{ span an isosceles triangle}\bigr\}.$$

It is known that $\varphi(n,3,3) < n\cdot 2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}$ (via Behrend-type sets on a line), and it has been conjectured that $\varphi(n,3,3)/n \to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$.

Determine the asymptotic order of $\varphi(n,3,3)$ as $n\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The asymptotic order of φ(n,3,3) remains open. Erdős conjectured that φ(n,3,3)/n → ∞, but even this superlinear lower bound has not been established; the only known upper bound is the Behrend-type n·2^{O(√log n)}, while no nontrivial lower bound beyond linear is known. Recent surveys and problem collections on Erdős distance problems still list this as open.

status_evidence.claim: The problem of determining the minimum number of distinct distances among n planar points spanning no isosceles triangle is listed among open Erdős distance problems.

status_evidence.title: Point Sets with Few Distinct Distances – Some Plane Truths (A. Sheffer)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of φ(n,3,3) and the Behrend-type construction giving n·2^{O(√log n)}; Erdős conjectured the count is ω(n), still unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Only an n·2^{O(√log n)} upper bound is known, and Erdős's conjecture φ(n,3,3) = ω(n) remains unproven.
